reasoning_summary: Previous SVR settings repeatedly overfit with an RBF kernel and moderate C. This grid shifts toward lower C and higher epsilon to reduce model flexibility, while also testing linear and polynomial kernels and a small set of gamma values to see whether simpler or less localized decision functions improve CV generalization.
search_strategy: Constrain the search to a compact grid emphasizing regularization and reduced sensitivity: lower C values, broader epsilon values, and a mix of kernels including linear, rbf, and poly. For rbf/poly, include both scale/auto and a few numeric gamma values spanning weak to moderate locality. Keep the grid under the candidate limit while exploring simpler models first.
expected_effect_on_overfitting: Likely to reduce overfitting by lowering model capacity through smaller C and larger epsilon, and by allowing linear kernel options that are less prone to fitting noise than RBF with higher effective complexity.
expected_effect_on_underfitting: May slightly increase underfitting risk for the smallest C and largest epsilon settings, especially with linear kernel; the inclusion of moderate C and RBF/poly options should help recover fit if the data needs nonlinearity.
computational_cost_estimate: 60 candidates total (5 x 4 x 5 x 3), which is within the 120-candidate limit and modest for n_train=21.
warnings: Poly kernel can be sensitive on small datasets; if instability appears, prefer linear or rbf results.
Numeric gamma values are included only for rbf/poly; linear kernel will ignore gamma in sklearn SVR, but it is kept in the grid for completeness of the search space.
